summary: Armenia is visa-free for a broad range of passports — the EU, UK, US, Russia, Japan, the Gulf states and several other CIS and Latin American countries can stay up to 180 days in a year, and China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay up to 90 days — while most other nationalities can apply online for an e-Visa, and some can also get a visa at the border. A smaller group of nationalities must apply through an embassy with an invitation. From 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, nationals of 111 listed countries who hold a US, EU, Schengen or Gulf residence permit can enter without a visa.

defaultStayWindow.text: The MFA states that citizens of countries with a visa-free regime “can stay on the territory of the Republic of Armenia for no more than 180 days during one year if no other term is defined by the international agreements”. It does not say how the year is counted or whether the days of arrival and departure are counted.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia — Visa

conditionalWaivers.text: From 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, nationals of 111 listed countries who hold a residence permit issued by the US, an EU or Schengen state, the UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait or Oman, valid for at least six months from entry, can enter without a visa and stay up to 180 days in a year. The permit must be a physical card or a passport sticker showing, in Latin script, the document title, name, nationality, date of birth and validity dates.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia — Temporary visa exemption: list of 111 countries (30 June 2026)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for every visitor to Armenia. The Foreign Ministry's visa checker lists travel (medical) insurance among the mandatory documents for some nationalities' visa applications (for example India) and among the documents to provide if available for others (for example Canada).

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward or return ticket requirement for every visitor to Armenia. The Foreign Ministry's visa checker lists an air ticket reservation with return among the mandatory documents for some nationalities' visa applications (for example India), and says a one-way ticket is sufficient for those arriving for education or work or in other justified cases.

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement for every visitor to Armenia, or an amount. The Foreign Ministry's visa checker lists proof of financial means (a bank statement for the last 3 months, a certificate of employment with salary, a work contract or other proof) among the mandatory documents for some nationalities' visa applications (for example India).

notes: The Government of Canada notes that the import and export of cultural and historical items is regulated in Armenia, including archaeological objects, sculptures and paintings, ancient books and documents, musical instruments, furniture and carpets.

safety.text: The UK says crime levels are low, with occasional pickpocketing, bag-snatching, theft from cars and burglary involving foreign nationals. It advises against all travel within 5 km of the entire eastern border with Azerbaijan, which remains closed, and along the M16/H26 road between Ijevan and Noyemberyan.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The Government of Canada describes Armenia's climate as continental: in Yerevan summers are hot and winters mild, while much of the country lies above 1,000 m, where it is cooler and rainfall is more frequent. The rainy season generally runs from March to June and from October to November, when seasonal flooding can disrupt overland travel.

tips.text: According to the UK Foreign Office, Armenia's land borders with Turkey and Azerbaijan are closed, although there are scheduled direct flights between Yerevan and Istanbul; the border with Iran is open to foreign nationals coming from Iran, though this can change at short notice.
The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel within 5 km of Armenia's entire eastern border with Azerbaijan, and along the M16/H26 road between Ijevan and Noyemberyan, because of border tensions.
The UK Foreign Office warns that hailing taxis on the street risks being scammed for high fares, and calls the GG taxi app a reputable service in Armenia.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Armenia?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Russia, Japan, the Gulf states and several other CIS and Latin American countries enter visa-free and can stay up to 180 days in a year; citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay can stay up to 90 days. Most other nationalities can apply online for an e-Visa (21 or 120 days) and some can also get a visa at the border; some nationalities need an invitation and must apply through an embassy. From 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, nationals of 111 listed countries who hold a residence permit from the US, an EU or Schengen state or a Gulf state (the UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait or Oman), valid for at least six months from entry, can enter without a visa for up to 180 days in a year.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Armenia visa-free?
faq.answer: Most visa-waiver nationalities may stay up to 180 days in total within one year. Citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay get up to 90 days under their own agreements.

faq.question: Can I get an Armenian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: For some nationalities. Some — including Canada — can get a visitor visa at the border outright, according to the Foreign Ministry's visa checker. Most other e-Visa nationalities qualify on arrival only if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the EU or Schengen states, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia or Japan, or a residence permit from a Gulf state; the Foreign Ministry lists none for Taiwanese passports. The Foreign Ministry recommends applying online in advance at evisa.mfa.am.

faq.question: Is the land border between Armenia and Turkey open?
faq.answer: No. According to the UK Foreign Office the land border with Turkey is closed, although there are scheduled direct flights between Yerevan and Istanbul, and the border with Azerbaijan is closed too.
